photos.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit — color correction only.
Asset: a corrected still photograph to replace the first photo in a video.

Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the original 4:3 photograph of a real handmade block-shaped figure held in a person's hand. Image 2 is a COLOR REFERENCE ONLY: a frame from the last second of the finished video showing the same figure on a white rotating platform.

Correct ONLY the colors, tonal balance, and exposure of the figure in image 1 so it matches the physical figure's colors in image 2. The reference is authoritative: the face and arms are warm peach/amber-orange, the shirt's dark pixels are neutral charcoal-black, the patterned yellow/gold pixels are warm golden yellow, and the trousers are visibly lighter muted gray-green/olive charcoal, NOT near-black saturated emerald green. Lift the crushed trouser shadows enough to see the gray-green material and separate both legs while retaining depth. Match the reference's naturally lit colors and restrained saturation, without a dramatic filter. The hair remains natural charcoal-black, with visible real material texture.

Preserve image 1's EXACT original viewing angle, camera framing, perspective, pose, facial pixel arrangement, hair silhouette, all clothing pixel patterns, proportions, paper seams, edge imperfections, and the full supporting human hand. The target figure's arms remain hanging down as in image 1: do NOT copy the raised-arm pose from the reference. Do not add a platform, remove the hand, change the face, restage the photo, redraw the product, or turn it into CGI. Keep the original gray photographic backdrop and realistic hand skin tones. Treat the reference as color guidance, not as a composition, lighting-direction or pose template.

Output just ONE edited 4:3 photograph matching image 1's composition, with its complete head, arms, legs and feet preserved. Prefer the original 4032×3024 canvas, or another high-resolution 4:3 canvas with exactly the same framing. No text, arrows, logos, borders, glow, extra objects or new design details. This is a faithful color retouch of the supplied photo, not a new product render.

Use case: precise-object-edit — color correction only.
Asset: a corrected still photograph to replace the second opening photo in a video.

Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the original 4:3 three-quarter side photograph of the handmade block-shaped figure held in a human hand. Image 2 is the authoritative COLOR REFERENCE from the last second of the finished video. Image 3 is the already color-corrected FRONT photograph of this same figure, supplied only to keep the two edited stills in one consistent photographic color family.

Correct ONLY the figure's colors, tonal balance and exposure in image 1 to match images 2 and 3: warm peach/amber-orange face and arms; neutral charcoal-black hair and dark shirt pixels; warm golden-yellow patterned shirt pixels; visibly lighter, desaturated gray-green/olive-charcoal trousers rather than the original crushed near-black emerald-green trousers. Retain natural shadow depth and visible paper texture. In particular, the trouser color and brightness should closely match the trousers in image 3 and the final-video reference. Use restrained realistic saturation.

Keep image 1's EXACT original three-quarter side angle, pose, camera perspective, proportions, face and hair pixels, clothing pattern, paper seams, full supporting hand, skin tones, gray photographic background and overall 4:3 composition. All head, arms and feet remain visible. Do not change it into the front-facing view of image 3. Its arms stay down, exactly as in image 1; do NOT copy the raised-arm pose or rotating platform from image 2. Do not redesign or re-render the product as CGI, clean away physical seams, replace the hand, alter anatomy, add objects, or change the backdrop.

Return just ONE edited 4:3 photo with the same framing, preferably the original 4032×3024 canvas or another high-resolution 4:3 canvas. No text, arrows, borders, logos, glow, or new details. This is a faithful color retouch of image 1.

notes: Both edited images exported on the original 4032×3024 canvas so landscape/portrait crop coordinates are retained. The first photo is reused by the ending scene.
